title: Pipecat Playground
summary: Build a real voice bot one Pipecat feature at a time, right in your browser. Each tab adds something (turn-taking, new voices and LLMs, tools, a Flow) and you talk to it as it grows, watching every frame and the matching bot.py. Bring your own free Deepgram key.
detail: The opener for our Pipecat series. You build one live bot across seven tabs: give it a personality, tune how it knows you’ve finished talking, swap its ears, brain and voice, give it tools that really run, turn it into a Pipecat Flow, watch its frames like Whisker does, then download the bot.py and run it yourself. It runs on your own Deepgram key in the browser; nothing to install.
outcome: A working voice bot you built yourself, plus the Pipecat bot.py that does the same job on your machine.
artifact: Your own bot.py: Pipecat code for the bot you built, ready to run locally or deploy to Pipecat Cloud.
prereqs: A laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari, and a microphone (headphones help)
A free Deepgram API key from console.deepgram.com ($200 credit, no card needed)

flow.title: Open the playground
flow.note: Self-guided. Go station by station, or jump to the one you care about.

sections.title: Try it
sections.summary: Open the playground, then work through the stations along the top.

steps.title: Open the Pipecat Playground
steps.instruction: Open https://dgeventhub.com/pipecat-playground/ in a new tab. Paste your Deepgram key in the box on the right and press Start my bot. Allow the microphone.
steps.check: Your bot greets you and answers when you talk.

steps.title: 01 Say hello
steps.instruction: Give your bot a name, a greeting and a system prompt, then talk to it. Watch the frames hop through its pipeline and check the latency of each turn. Ask for a long story and talk over it to see an interruption.
steps.check: You can point to where speech becomes text and where text becomes speech.

steps.title: 02 Turn-taking
steps.instruction: Watch your call on the timeline. Move eot_threshold and eot_timeout_ms, apply, and try pausing mid-sentence.
steps.check: You can say why a pause in the middle of a sentence doesn’t end your turn.

steps.title: 03 Swap services
steps.instruction: Switch your bot’s speech-to-text, LLM and voice while you talk to it, and watch which lines of bot.py change.
steps.check: You’ve seen that swapping a provider is about one line.

steps.title: 04 Function calling
steps.instruction: Turn on tools (weather, time, dice, notes, page color, hang up) and ask for things that need them. Follow each call step by step.
steps.check: You can explain how the LLM decides to call a tool and what comes back.

steps.title: 05 Pipecat Flows
steps.instruction: Switch on the Flow and order pizza or sushi. Watch the conversation move from node to node and the kitchen ticket fill in.
steps.check: You can see which functions each node allows.

steps.title: 06 and 07: Watch it run, then ship it
steps.instruction: Click through every frame your bot produced, like Whisker shows. Add Whisker or Tail to bot.py, pick how people reach your bot, and download bot.py.
steps.check: You have a bot.py you can run.

steps.title: 08 What else?
steps.instruction: Browse the 22 things people build with Pipecat. Each card names the real example file in the Pipecat repo (https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) so you can start from it.
steps.check: You’ve picked one thing you want to build next.

troubleshooting: No answer: check the key box for an error, and that you allowed the microphone in the address bar.
The bot hears itself and keeps talking: use headphones.
No mic? Type in the box under your key instead.
Your key is only used in that tab. It’s swapped for a 30-second token and never saved.
